title: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment…
paragraphs: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment…
The garden is quiet. Morning light rests gently on the leaves. Nothing feels broken yet. Then I hear it — a whisper that doesn’t shout, doesn’t threaten… just questions:

I stand still, watching from a distance. I am a witness, not a biblical character. Yet the question feels strangely familiar. It isn’t loud rebellion. It’s subtle distortion. A soft reframing. A seed of doubt planted in perfect peace.
The serpent doesn’t deny God outright — it nudges truth sideways. And I realize… temptation often begins not with defiance, but with doubt.
What if the first battle was not about fruit — but about trust?
In the quiet spaces of my own life, I sometimes hear echoes of that whisper. Questions that blur clarity. Thoughts that slightly bend what I know to be true.
What whispers try to distort truth in my life today?
